For the duration, you sense the presence of magical effects within 30 feet of yourself. If you sense such effects, you can take the @action[Magic|XPHB] action to see a faint aura around any visible creature or object in the area that bears the magic, and if an effect was created by a spell, you learn the spell's school of magic.

The spell is blocked by 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead.
Briefly surrounded by silvery mist, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
You have &Reference[rule=Darkvision] with a range of 60 feet.

You are part of a lineage that grants you supernatural abilities. You know the @UUID[.k9FLRL4sK39AA2m4] cantrip. Whenever you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you can replace that cantrip with a different cantrip from the Wizard spell list.

When you reach character level 3, you learn the @UUID[.rESEZPWh0Wv6grZk] spell. When you reach character level 5, you also learn the @UUID[.yUrur1DUF707spJg] spell. You always have these spells prepared, and you can cast each spell once without a spell slot. Once you cast either of these spells with this trait, you can't cast that spell with it again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB]. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.

Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this trait (choose the ability when you select the lineage).
You have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on saving throws you make to avoid or end the &Reference[condition=Charmed] condition.
You have proficiency in the &Reference[skill=Insight], &Reference[skill=Perception], or &Reference[skill=Survival] skill.

You don't need to sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep. You can finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB] in 4 hours if you spend those hours in a trancelike meditation, during which you retain consciousness.

Created by the god Corellon, the first elves could change their forms at will. They lost this ability when Corellon cursed them for plotting with the deity Lolth, who tried and failed to usurp Corellon's dominion. When Lolth was cast into the Abyss, most elves renounced her and earned Corellon's forgiveness, but that which Corellon had taken from them was lost forever.

No longer able to shape-shift at will, the elves retreated to the Feywild, where their sorrow was deepened by that plane's influence. Over time, curiosity led many of them to explore other planes of existence, including worlds in the Material Plane.

Elves have pointed ears and lack facial and body hair. They live for around 750 years, and they don't sleep but instead enter a trance when they need to rest. In that state, they remain aware of their surroundings while immersing themselves in memories and meditations.

An environment subtly transforms elves after they inhabit it for a millennium or more, and it grants them certain kinds of magic. Drow, high elves, and wood elves are examples of elves who have been transformed thus.

Drow

Drow typically dwell in the Underdark and have been shaped by it. Some drow individuals and societies avoid the Underdark altogether yet carry its magic. In the Eberron setting, for example, drow dwell in rainforests and cyclopean ruins on the continent of Xen'drik.

High Elves

High elves have been infused with the magic of crossings between the Feywild and the Material Plane. On some worlds, high elves refer to themselves by other names. For example, they call themselves sun or moon elves in the Forgotten Realms setting, Silvanesti and Qualinesti in the Dragonlance setting, and Aereni in the Eberron setting.

Wood Elves

Wood elves carry the magic of primeval forests within themselves. They are known by many other names, including wild elves, green elves, and forest elves. Grugach are reclusive wood elves of the Greyhawk setting, while the Kagonesti and the Tairnadal are wood elves of the Dragonlance and Eberron settings, respectively.

You are connected to one of the dragonmarked houses, but you haven't (yet) manifested a dragonmark. You might be a member of the family by birth or an employee of the house with no familial connection. You've earned your living by doing the business of the house, serving as the hands, feet, and eyes of house leadership in the world. You might have many old friends, mentors, and rivals in the house you serve, plus allies or enemies in other houses.

  • Feat: @feat[Lucky|XPHB]

You gain the following benefits.

Luck Points. You have a number of Luck Points equal to your @variantrule[Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus] and can spend the points on the benefits below. You regain your expended Luck Points when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Advantage. When you roll a [[/r d20]] for a @variantrule[D20 Test|XPHB], you can spend 1 Luck Point to give yourself @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on the roll.

Disadvantage. When a creature rolls a [[/r d20]] for an attack roll against you, you can spend 1 Luck Point to impose @variantrule[Disadvantage|XPHB] on that roll.

A master of preparation and battlefield foresight. The Tactician uses Intelligence to outmaneuver foes and empower allies through carefully laid plans.

Primary Ability: Intelligence (then Dexterity)
Your learning encompasses far more than simply warfare. You learn two languages of your choice.
You rely on predictive measures and careful observation to protect yourself, rather than raw agility. You can use your Intelligence instead of your Dexterity when determining your Armor Class.

You can spend 10 minutes formulating a Perfect Plan, gaining Perfect Plan dice (d4s) equal to your Intelligence modifier (min 1). The plan includes yourself and any number of willing creatures within 60 ft when made.

When a creature within 60 ft that is part of your plan makes a d20 Test and can see or hear you, you can use your Reaction to expend one Perfect Plan die, adding it to the result. You may decide after the d20 is rolled but before success/failure is announced. Only one die at a time; a rolled die is lost.

Once made, you can't make another plan until you finish a Long Rest, at which point unspent dice are lost.

Level 5+: Max dice = Intelligence modifier + Proficiency Bonus (min 4).
You can use the Mastery property of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the weapons chosen.
A Backpack holds up to 30 pounds within 1 cubic foot. It can also serve as a saddlebag.
A Quiver holds up to 20 Arrows.

After drinking this potion, you can take a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB] to exhale fire at a target within 30 feet of yourself. The target makes a [[/save ability=dex dc=13]] saving throw, taking [[/damage 4d6 type=fire]] damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. The effect ends after you exhale the fire three times or when 1 hour has passed.

This potion's orange liquid flickers, and smoke fills the top of the container and wafts out whenever it is opened.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.phbagAmmunitionV]{Ammunition} is required by a weapon that has the Ammunition property. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon. The Ammunition table lists the different types and the amount you get when you buy them. The table also lists the item that is typically used to store each type; storage must be bought separately.

You create a magical effect within range. Choose the effect from the options below. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its non-instantaneous effects active at a time.

Sensory Effect. You create an instantaneous, harmless sensory effect, such as a shower of sparks, a puff of wind, faint musical notes, or an odd odor.

Fire Play. You instantaneously light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a small campfire.

Clean or Soil. You instantaneously clean or soil an object no larger than 1 cubic foot.

Minor Sensation. You chill, warm, or flavor up to 1 cubic foot of nonliving material for 1 hour.

Magic Mark. You make a color, a small mark, or a symbol appear on an object or a surface for 1 hour.

Minor Creation. You create a nonmagical trinket or an illusory image that can fit in your hand. It lasts until the end of your next turn. A trinket can deal no damage and has no monetary worth.

As a Bonus Action, begin analyzing a creature you can see within 60 ft. While analyzing:

  • You gain a special extra Reaction once each round (not on the same turn as your normal Reaction), usable only to spend Perfect Plan dice on d20 Tests made against, in contest with, or caused by the analyzed creature.
  • The analyzed creature has Disadvantage on opportunity attacks against you.

Lasts 1 minute. Ends early if you lose Concentration, or if you end your turn unable to see it or more than 60 ft away.
When you complete a Short Rest, you can regain expended Perfect Plan dice equal to half your maximum (rounded up). Once used, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.
A set of clothes worn by travellers.

You touch a creature that has died within the last minute. That creature revives with 1 Hit Point. This spell can't revive a creature that has died of old age, nor does it restore any missing body parts.
You gain Expertise in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. You gain this feature again at level 10.
A Tactician who courts fortune — pushing Perfect Plan dice for bigger payoffs, bluffing through any situation, and bending luck when it won't cooperate.
You gain proficiency in two of: Deception, Insight, or Sleight of Hand. Additionally, you gain proficiency with up to two gaming sets of your choice.

Once per turn, when you roll a Perfect Plan die, you can double down: roll it again and add that roll to the result. If you roll a 1 on the new roll, note it.

Once you have noted a number of 1s equal to your Proficiency Bonus, you can't use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest (noted 1s then reset to 0).

All In. When you add a Perfect Plan die to a creature's attack roll, you can declare that attack an All In.

  • if the total of the attack roll equals or exceeds the target's AC + 15 + the target's Proficiency Bonus, the attack is a critical hit

  • Otherwise, the attack resolves normally

Pay the Debt. If you declare All In and fail to force a critical hit, you must spend Perfect Plan dice one at a time - rolling each and adding it to a running total - until that total exceeds 4. if you fail to do so, you can't declare All In again until you finish a Short Rest.
